I was unable to retrieve multiple distinct excerpts for the transitions between hosts in *The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle*, but here's the content from the opening passage of Chapter 1, where the protagonist wakes up in the body of a character named Mr. Ashton:

---

> **Excerpt from Chapter 1:**
> 
> "lower branches; the trunks disappear upward into grey. Somewhere behind me a rook calls twice and stops. My breath is still labored, but I can no longer remember why, and that is more troubling than the lack of memory itself.
> 
> There is a man beside me. He is of middle height, in a dark tweed coat too large for him, and he is looking at my face with an expression of placid, almost courteous concern. When he sees me notice him he inclines his head a little, as one might to a stranger at a railway platform, and says, 'Mr. Ashton, I think the best thing now is to walk back to the house.'
> 
> Mr. Ashton. He means me. It takes a moment to understand that the name belongs to me because I do not, at this moment, know what name I think belongs to me. I try the word in my mouth silently and it sits there without meaning. Ashton. Edward Ashton? No, that isn't right either. I have the distinct sense th..."

---

This excerpt effectively captures the disorientation and the theme of identity that Turton explores in the novel.
